profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC2 sits at 44621 Waxpool Road, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total that CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, so it is not applied to this specific building's own capacity figure, and no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC2 was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ markets a "campus within a campus" concept at LC, allowing customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record, though this is not independently confirmed for CloudHQ specifically.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators, including Amazon Web Services, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and Centersquare/Csquare facilities, within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing footprint.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC2 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, a site the operator describes as sitting in the densest concentration of fiber in the world. The full campus totals 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of critical IT load across all fourteen buildings, with 756 megawatts currently available. CloudHQ does not publish a capacity figure specific to LC2 itself, so the contribution of this individual building to the campus total cannot be determined from operator sources or independent aggregators.

Ashburn hosts the largest concentration of data center capacity globally, with dozens of competing operators within a few miles of the LC Campus, including AWS, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and others. The entire LC Campus, if ranked as a single facility against published Virginia capacity, would rank 24th in the state by megawatts, though Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities of which only 23 publish capacity figures. The utility supplier for LC2 is not named by CloudHQ; Dominion Energy serves the county broadly but is not confirmed as the operator's supplier.

Without building-level capacity published for LC2, this facility cannot be assessed in isolation as a discrete constraint on or opportunity for AI scaling. To understand LC2's role in the grid or compute ecosystem, one would need either CloudHQ to break out per-building capacity, third-party measurement of the building's power draw, or disclosure of LC2's contracted tenants and their workloads.
